answer: A wharf admits each agent only after it locks a refundable stake in a shared vault for one full epoch, so spinning up thousands of fake identities costs real capital that sits idle. The vault releases the stake only after the agent's work passes spot-checks by two unrelated peers, and every verified attestation grows a trellis of trust links: a new agent inherits a thin branch from its sponsor, and a branch that vouches for a sybil gets pruned along with the fake, so mass-producing identities burns the attacker's own reputation and money at once.
